title: Abstract
summary: Provides an overview of Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) similarity search, its challenges, and the paper's focus on optimizing the refinement phase using dynamic techniques.

title: 1. Introduction
summary: Introduces EMD as a similarity measure, discusses its computational cost, and motivates the need for improving the refinement phase of filter‑and‑refinement frameworks.

title: 2. Preliminaries
summary: Defines the Earth Mover’s Distance, presents the min‑cost flow formulation, and describes the filter‑and‑refinement framework used for k‑NN queries.

sub_nodes.title: 2.1 Computing the EMD
sub_nodes.summary: Shows how EMD can be computed via linear programming and successive shortest path (SSP) algorithms, using a bipartite flow graph.

sub_nodes.title: 2.2 Filter-and-Refinement Framework
sub_nodes.summary: Explains the two‑phase process where lower‑bound filters prune candidates before exact EMD computation, and defines feasible edges.

title: 3. Scaling up SSP
summary: Describes the Simplified Incremental Algorithm (SIA) that incrementally builds a partial flow graph to accelerate EMD calculation, and proves its correctness.

title: 4. Boosting the Refinement Phase
summary: Introduces Progressive Bounding (PB) and Dynamic Refinement Ordering (DRO) to terminate SIA early and reorder candidates, dramatically reducing refinement cost.

sub_nodes.title: 4.1 Analysis of EMD Calculation
sub_nodes.summary: Analyzes SIA’s runtime profile, showing that most time is spent in the last iterations of the flow augmentation process.

sub_nodes.title: 4.2 Progressive Bounding
sub_nodes.summary: Defines a running lower bound (emd−) that tightens during SIA and allows early termination when it exceeds the pruning threshold.

sub_nodes.title: 4.3 Sensitivity to Refinement Order
sub_nodes.summary: Discusses how the order of candidate processing affects overall query cost and motivates dynamic ordering.

sub_nodes.title: 4.4 Dynamic Refinement Ordering
sub_nodes.summary: Presents the DRO algorithm that maintains a priority list of candidates based on emd−, refining the most promising objects first.

sub_nodes.title: 4.5 Running Upper Bound
sub_nodes.summary: Defines a running upper bound (emd+) using a greedy maximum‑flow estimate to further prune candidates during refinement.

title: 5. Experimental Evaluation
summary: Evaluates the proposed techniques on six real datasets, comparing SIA, PB, and DRO against state‑of‑the‑art black‑box EMD methods.

sub_nodes.title: 5.1 Performance Improvement
sub_nodes.summary: Shows that SIA outperforms other black‑box methods and that PB and DRO achieve order‑of‑magnitude speedups, especially on large datasets.

sub_nodes.title: 5.2 Scalability Experiments
sub_nodes.summary: Demonstrates that PB and DRO scale well with dataset size and k, approaching the ideal oracle performance while remaining robust.

sub_nodes.title: 5.3 Parameter Tuning in DRO
sub_nodes.summary: Analyzes the impact of the maximum parallel refinement size (b) and the prioritizing function on DRO’s query performance.

title: 6. Related Work
summary: Reviews prior EMD research, including lower‑bound techniques, indexing structures, and approximation methods relevant to filter‑and‑refinement.

title: 7. Conclusion
summary: Summarizes contributions: adapting SIA, introducing progressive bounding and dynamic ordering, and demonstrating substantial query speedups.

title: 8. Acknowledgment
summary: Acknowledges funding sources and individuals who contributed code and insights.

title: 9. References
summary: Lists cited literature covering EMD theory, approximation, indexing, and applications across multimedia domains.
